title: The C Major Scale
description: The C major scale is the foundation of Western music: eight whole-and-half steps with no sharps or flats. Every pianist learns it first because the pattern of tones and semitones it teaches — W-W-H-W-W-W-H — repeats in every major key. This record plays it ascending at 100 BPM.

title: The A Natural Minor Scale
description: A natural minor shares its key signature with C major but starts on A, giving music its sadder, darker color. The pattern W-H-W-W-H-W-W is the relative-minor twin of the major scale. Played here ascending at 100 BPM.

title: Twelve-Bar Blues in C
description: The twelve-bar blues is the chassis of rock, jazz, and R&B: twelve bars cycling I–I–I–I–IV–IV–I–I–V–IV–I–V. Each chord below is a dominant-seventh voicing held one full bar at 96 BPM, exactly how a rhythm section comps it.

title: Ode to Joy — Beethoven
description: Beethoven's Ninth Symphony finale (1824) gave the world the most-sung melody ever written, and it is long out of copyright. The opening phrase climbs stepwise E–E–F–G, the textbook example of a folk-like classical theme. Played at 110 BPM.

title: A Minor Pentatonic Scale
description: Five notes — A, C, D, E, G — power nearly all rock and blues lead guitar. The minor pentatonic cannot clash badly with a minor-key backing track, which is why beginners solo with it first. Ascending and descending at 100 BPM.

title: Jazz ii–V–I in C
description: The ii–V–I cadence is jazz's home base: Dm7 pulls to G7, which resolves to Cmaj7. Every jazz standard is stitched from these. The voicings below are root-position seventh chords, two bars each at 90 BPM.

title: Minuet in G — Opening
description: The famous Minuet in G (BWV Anh. 114, long attributed to Bach, actually by Christian Petzold) is the world's most-played beginner piano piece and firmly public domain. Its opening pickup climbs D–G–A–B–C–D in bright triple feel at 120 BPM.

title: Reggae One-Drop Skank in C
description: Reggae's one-drop drops the downbeat: the kick and snare land together on beat 3 while the guitar skanks short offbeat chops. This record renders the skank pattern — muted C-major chops on the offbeats at 76 BPM.

title: Twinkle Twinkle Little Star
description: The melody Mozart used for his K.265 variations began life as the French folk song 'Ah! vous dirai-je, maman'. Six notes — C–C–G–G–A–A–G — teach every child intervals before they know the word. Played at 100 BPM.

title: Air on the G String — Motif
t: Air on the G String — Motif
description: Bach's Orchestral Suite No. 3, Air (BWV 1068), arranged for violin on the G string, is the most famous slow melody in classical music and public domain. The opening sighs downward in D major at a stately 66 BPM.

title: Raga Bhairav — Arohana
description: Bhairav is a dawn raga of Hindustani classical music built on S–r–G–m–P–d–N: a major scale with flattened second and sixth, giving it a devotional gravity. The ascending line (arohana) is rendered here at 80 BPM.

title: Waltz Bass Pattern in A Minor
t: Waltz Bass Pattern in A Minor
description: The Viennese waltz engine is bass–chord–chord in 3/4: one low root, then two soft chord pillows. Chopin and Strauss both ride it. This A-minor loop runs at 140 BPM with the bass on beat one.

title: Fugue Subject in D Minor
description: A fugue subject announces the theme alone, then voices pile in imitating it — Bach's signature architecture. This D-minor subject rises stepwise, leaps, and cadences on the raised seventh, in Baroque style at 100 BPM.

title: Pachelbel Canon Progression
description: Pachelbel's Canon (c. 1694) is eight chords — D–A–Bm–F#m–G–D–G–A — under a bass that never changes, and pop music has quoted it for three centuries. Bass line plus the canon's opening melody phrase at 72 BPM.
